title: Fifty, then five
told: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there anything you stop for every single day, no matter what?
options: ha. a good ritual. today, one that comes five times.
then you know the pull of it. listen.
that’s okay. here’s a day built around five stops.

steps.line: One night, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells, he was taken from Mecca to Jerusalem, and from there up through the heavens.
There, God gave him a gift for his people: fifty prayers, every day.
On his way back he met Musa, Moses. “Your people can’t manage that,” Musa told him. “Go back and ask for less.”

steps.q: He goes back and asks. What do you think happens?
o: It comes down step by step
steps.why: Back and forth, again and again. The tellings differ on the steps, by five, by ten or by half, but each time it came down, until it was five.

steps.line: He went back, and the number came down. Musa sent him again, and again, until it was five.

steps.q: Why might Musa have kept sending him back to ask?
o: He thought fifty was too few
He had seen how hard it is for people to keep up
He wanted each prayer to be shorter
steps.why: In one telling Musa says he had already tried it with his own people. The prayer was meant to fit people who can actually keep it.

steps.line: “They are five,” God said, “and they are fifty.” Five prayers a day, with the reward of fifty.

steps.q: At five, Musa urges him to go back once more. What does he say?
o: He’s too shy to ask again
He goes, and it becomes three
He says five is exactly right
steps.why: In the hadith he says, “I have asked my Lord until I feel shy.” Five stayed, and so did the reward of fifty.

steps.line: The five follow the sun: Fajr before sunrise, Dhuhr after midday, Asr in the afternoon, Maghrib after sunset, Isha at night.
Today, in a stockroom at lunch, a man stands, bows, then sets his forehead on a flattened box. A saying teaches: here, a person is nearest to God.
steps.label: today

steps.q: A saying of the Prophet ﷺ explains why a stockroom floor works. What does it say?
o: Pray only where no one can see you
Any room becomes a mosque at the call
The whole earth is made a place of prayer
steps.why: “The earth has been made for me a mosque, and pure,” says the hadith. Any clean spot will do, which is why a prayer mat, or a flattened box, travels well.

say: here’s what i love. the gift started as fifty, and kept being made lighter until people could carry it. and nothing was lost.
in islam, salat is a set shape at set times: standing, bowing, forehead to the ground. the body prays too, five times a day, following the sun.

steps.q: The prayers came down from fifty to five, yet God said “they are fifty.” What does that tell you?
o: Each of the five counts like ten
The other forty-five are still owed later
You should pray fifty times anyway
steps.why: Five to keep, the reward of fifty: each one counts tenfold. Many read it as mercy built right into the number.

today.say: today, notice where the sun is at five moments: before sunrise, after midday, afternoon, sunset, night. it’s your choice: just notice, look up the prayer times where you live, or try one slow bow yourself.
options: lovely. the day already has a shape.
good. you’ll see them move with the seasons.

sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (the Night Journey: fifty prayers enjoined; Musa: “your followers cannot bear it,” go back; reduced in stages; “These are five and they are fifty; the word does not change with Me”)
Sahih Muslim 162 (the same account, reduced by five at a time)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 and Sahih Muslim 162 (Musa: “I have tested people before you,” the Children of Israel)
Qur’an 17:1 (the journey by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque)
Sahih Muslim 482 (a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating)
Sunan Abi Dawud 393; Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 149 (the times of the five prayers)
Sahih Muslim 162 (“five prayers every day and night, each counted as ten, so that makes fifty”)
check: The versions differ on how the number came down (“a part” in Bukhari 349, by tens in 3207, by five in Muslim 162); captions say only that it “came down”. Bukhari 349 does not mention Jerusalem; caption 1 follows Muslim 162 and Qur’an 17:1. Confirm.
Paintings show Mecca and the heavens with no people and no Buraq; Jerusalem is named but not painted. Confirm.
